title: Junichiro Jackson
hook: A grief-haunted fighter and his partner cross a monster-ridden near-future Brooklyn.

media.title: Watch the submitted Junichiro Jackson source video
media.attribution: Embedded from the fan-submitted public YouTube source; Audience Take does not rehost the video.
media.accessibleFallback: Open the submitted source on YouTube if the embedded player is unavailable.

storyContext.summary: The submitted material presents a genre story centered on a fighter, his partner, and a dangerous near-future Brooklyn setting.
storyContext.storyworld: A near-future Brooklyn where supernatural danger intersects with action, grief, and a hip-hop-influenced visual identity.
storyContext.currentFormat: Public concept video submitted for scouting

creatorContext.summary: The creator has not claimed this fan-nominated Scout Card, so creator identity and project status require direct verification.
limitations: Audience Take has not verified a creator representative or received private project information.

evidenceClaims.statement: The submitted material presents a near-future Brooklyn storyworld combining hip-hop, anime-influenced imagery, and supernatural horror.
evidenceClaims.qualification: This characterization is based on the submitted public video and should not be read as creator-approved positioning.

pathways.label: Premium adult animated series
pathways.audience: Animation, manga, hip-hop, and psychological-horror audiences
pathways.rationale: A serialized format could test whether the Brooklyn storyworld and recurring relationships can sustain episodic development.
strengths: The submitted material presents a distinctive cultural and genre combination.
risks: The available public evidence does not yet show that the concept can sustain an episodic arc.
openQuestions: Which character relationship could anchor a first season?

nextExperiment.title: Pilot animatic audience test
nextExperiment.hypothesis: A short serialized proof may create stronger next-chapter intent than a standalone concept trailer.
nextExperiment.method: Release a clearly labeled animatic chapter and collect voluntary Audience Take responses.
nextExperiment.participantAction: Watch the chapter and state whether they would return for a second installment.
nextExperiment.signal: Completion and voluntary next-chapter intent, interpreted as an early signal rather than verified demand.

pathways.label: Independent animated feature
pathways.audience: Adult animation and independent genre-film audiences
pathways.rationale: A bounded feature could concentrate the central relationship and test whether the storyworld works as one complete arc.
strengths: A finite arc could make the project easier to evaluate as a single proof.
risks: Feature production scope may exceed what the currently visible public materials can support.
openQuestions: What complete emotional arc can the current concept resolve in feature length?

nextExperiment.title: Feature story-reel test
nextExperiment.hypothesis: A concise story reel may clarify whether the central arc is legible at feature scale.
nextExperiment.method: Create a short story reel covering setup, turning point, and ending without representing it as a finished film.
nextExperiment.participantAction: Watch the reel and identify the central conflict and expected resolution.
nextExperiment.signal: Comprehension and voluntary intent to watch a longer version, not acquisition probability.

pathways.label: Creator-direct serialized franchise
pathways.audience: Fans who follow creator-led worlds across episodes and illustrated releases
pathways.rationale: A creator-direct sequence of smaller releases could test the world in public while keeping each experiment bounded.
strengths: Smaller releases can isolate which characters and formats earn repeat attention.
risks: A multi-format cadence requires sustained creator capacity that has not been verified.
openQuestions: Which release format is practical for the creator to sustain?

nextExperiment.title: Two-part creator-direct release
nextExperiment.hypothesis: A paired animated and illustrated release may reveal which format best carries the storyworld.
nextExperiment.method: Publish two clearly connected free samples with the same narrative beat in different formats.
nextExperiment.participantAction: Choose which sample they would follow and explain why.
nextExperiment.signal: Format preference and return intent among voluntary participants.

limitations: This fixture contains no verified platform endorsement, private analytics, complete comment corpus, or native audience count.
Comparable-project citations remain an explicit research limitation in this representative contract fixture.

risks: The creator and current rights or production status have not been verified.
A concept video alone cannot establish sustained audience demand or production feasibility.
unresolvedQuestions: Which format can the creator realistically sustain?
What additional public evidence can substantiate creator and project history?
signalLimitations: No Audience Take-native participation is included in this contract fixture.
Public-web attention, if later observed, must remain separate from native commitments and votes.
